clue.text: Vile edict rewritten in other words

indicators.note: something rewritten has its contents set down afresh, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty decree has been redrafted, put another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns VILE EDICT into the Latin word used in legal texts and abbreviated viz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin adverb, shortened to viz., means namely, introducing a restatement.

clue.text: Rogue's not in residence

indicators.note: not here means the rogue word goes without the two letters named

parts.note: a rogue is a villain; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from VILLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country house or holiday home is a dwelling.

clue.text: Years hence, he's abandoned increasingly immoral behaviour

parts.note: a decade is a span of ten years

indicators.note: the word hence leaves behind the letters named

parts.note: he, with 's for 'is'

explanation.surface: From now on, a man has given up his worsening vices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Years hence' reads as a phrase about the future, but 'Years' is a piece on its own and 'abandoned' is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral decline or self-indulgent excess describes a society growing ever more corrupt.

clue.text: Enclosing letters composed many years ago

indicators.note: the letters of the word are composed afresh, set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wrote the letters in an envelope long before now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters composed' rearranges ENCLOSING.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a long time back, in the distant past.

clue.text: Time for giving present location in ocean?

definitions.text: Time for giving present location in ocean?

parts.words: Time for giving present location in ocean
parts.note: the festive season of gift-giving names a place surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: Asking about the festive gift-giving season and a place in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two such islands, one in the Indian Ocean and one in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The season for presents plus a piece of land in the sea names an Indian Ocean territory.

clue.text: Book for a long flight

parts.note: a flight is also a staircase, so a long one has many stairs; a John Buchan thriller title counts them

explanation.surface: A suggestion for a novel to read on a long-haul plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel, but it is a flight of stairs; John Buchan's spy novel is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Buchan's 1915 thriller is titled after a large number of stairs, a long flight of them.

clue.text: Conductor including one in experimental programme

definitions.meaning: a guide who steers ships through harbours, or someone who flies an aircraft
a trial episode made to test a television series before it is commissioned

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader takes part in a trial broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour guide steers vessels; a trial television episode tests whether a series is worth making.

clue.text: Offer for sale at a higher price

definitions.meaning: to place goods or property on the market
raised in cost, as prices are when increased

explanation.surface: Something is being sold for more money.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to place on the market and to raise, as with prices.

clue.text: Tree left somewhat affected

parts.note: arch means playfully knowing, a little affected in manner

explanation.surface: A tree has been abandoned, slightly damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' suggests harmed, but here it means putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Raised utter chaos over church clock?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the rest
in a down clue raised means turned upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to utter a sound is to emit it
pie is a printer's term for a jumble of type, hence chaos
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Total disorder breaks out in a church over its clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses the utter word in this down clue. Printer's pie is a heap of mixed-up type.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock is one kind of instrument for keeping time, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Account of heavenly body's crossing of empty space

indicators.note: the moon word lies across the account abbreviation, so it holds it within

parts.note: of the moon, the heavenly body, is lunar

explanation.surface: A report of a moon passing through a void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' is the container signal: the moon word goes over and around the abbreviation, which lands after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacuna is a gap, so the adjective describes something relating to a gap or blank space.

clue.text: Not staying healthy, having restricted energy

indicators.note: the healthy phrase confines the energy letter within its own letters

parts.note: someone in trim is fit and well
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone is unwell because they are short of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having restricted' puts E inside IN TRIM, after its T. 'Not staying' looks like a description of health but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provisional or temporary is meant only for a while, not to stay.

clue.text: Some of the grandest mountains

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is taken, so the answer sits among its letters

explanation.surface: A remark about the most impressive peaks in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' takes the run of letters across 'grandest'.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American range is one of the longest chains of peaks on Earth.

clue.text: Kentish rams by spring begin the business

parts.note: Kent is a county in South-East England, abbreviated SE
a tup is a ram, a male sheep
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: Kent's male sheep leap about as a farm starts trading.
explanation.walkthrough: KENT is a county in South-East England, hence SE. 'by' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a shop or start trading is an idiom for launching a commercial venture.

clue.text: Chapter by unknown author in accepted works

parts.note: anon., short for anonymous, marks a writer whose name is not known

explanation.surface: A chapter by an anonymous writer finds its way into a collection of classic texts.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's canon is the body of works generally agreed to be genuinely theirs.

clue.text: Guardian making you discount a misspelling?

indicators.note: a misspelling puts letters in the wrong order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper urges readers to overlook a typing error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelling' rearranges DISCOUNT A; 'making you' only links. Guardian is a newspaper, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper, such as a museum keeper or someone with legal charge of a child, is a guardian.

clue.text: Con oilmen about bend in rock strata

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil prospectors are swindled over a fold in the rock layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CON and OILMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the term for a single step-like fold where layers dip in one direction.

clue.text: List includes one record heard by jazz enthusiast

indicators.note: the spoken piece stands next to the fan word, after it

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz fan

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, so the spelling follows how they sound

parts.note: a log is a record, with a for one

explanation.surface: A list of items with a record heard by a jazz fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns A LOG into its sound-alike ALOGUE; 'includes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An itemised list of goods, books or works is a register or inventory.

clue.text: Awful rains are closing in right after the event

indicators.note: the jumbled letters close around the abbreviation, holding it
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Terrible rain is falling after the fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is the anagram signal; 'closing in' then wraps the jumbled letters around the right abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made in arrears is made at the end of a period, once the work or service is done.

clue.text: Writer who travelled giving endless service on the way

indicators.note: in an across clue the service word follows the way abbreviation

parts.note: ST, for street, is a way

indicators.note: the service word loses its final letter

parts.note: evensong is the Anglican evening service

explanation.surface: An author on a journey takes part in a never-ending church service while on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the G off EVENSONG. Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Travels with a Donkey in the Cévennes.
explanation.definitionFit: R. L. Stevenson wrote travel books, among them Travels with a Donkey, as well as novels.

clue.text: A minimal quantity run on time

indicators.note: in an across clue the run word is placed after the time letter

parts.note: to race is to run fast

explanation.surface: A tiny amount runs late.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount of something, barely detectable, is a hint or tiny remnant of it.

clue.text: Vehicles bound for Reading?

definitions.meaning: large passenger road vehicles, the full form of buses
bound volumes gathering several works together to be read

explanation.surface: Coaches are heading for the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading, capitalised, looks like the town in Berkshire, England; the second sense is about books bound for reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Large passenger buses and thick collected editions of an author's works share the same name.

clue.text: Relative hearing where many go on holiday

indicators.note: hearing signals that the place name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A relative hears about where crowds go for their vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' says the Riviera resort NICE is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: The two close to my small cottage

parts.note: both means the two of them together

indicators.note: close means the end, so the last letter of my is taken

explanation.surface: A pair live near my little house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' takes the Y of 'my'. A bothy is a Scottish hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a basic Scottish hut or shelter, a simple little dwelling.

clue.text: Vehicle's choice of side before end of motorway

indicators.note: the side choice comes ahead of the closing letter

parts.note: left or right, written L OR R

indicators.note: only the final letter of the road word is taken

explanation.surface: A truck has to choose a lane before the motorway finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle's' reads as 'Vehicle is'. 'end of' takes the Y of 'motorway'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large goods truck is a kind of road vehicle.

clue.text: Sing in special way unknown line at end of poem

indicators.note: the line letter comes after the poem word

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A singer performs oddly with a mystery line ending a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singing alternates rapidly between chest voice and falsetto, a distinctive vocal style.

clue.text: A matter of property? On the contrary, I earn it working

definitions.text: A matter of property? On the contrary

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone says their wages come from managing property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the phrase: not a matter of property but a property of matter. 'working' rearranges I EARN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance to change in motion is a basic physical property every bit of matter has.

clue.text: Antelope going across no good country

indicators.note: the antelope spans the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A useless antelope roams over the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going across' is the container signal: the antelope spans the no-good abbreviation, which lands after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the nations making up the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Poor finishing throughout when the side played badly

indicators.note: the final letter of every word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A team performed poorly in every match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing throughout' takes the last letters of 'when the side played badly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone short of money and necessities is in want, impoverished.

clue.text: Is spread around and left, in this?

definitions.text: Is spread around and left, in this?

indicators.note: around signals the letters being scattered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Things are scattered about and abandoned in this process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal, and the left abbreviation follows. Read whole, the clue also describes the act of scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattering things widely is spreading them out over an area.
